findings.message: The site requires a 'Sources' section in every post.
The site answered 403 (anti-bot or login wall): the link is inconclusive, not dead; open it by hand or use a browser check.

findings.quote: Around the winter solstice, Reykjavik gets about eleven hours of usable daylight.
findings.why: Reykjavik has only about four to five hours of daylight at the winter solstice, so readers planning December drives around an eleven-hour window could end up on icy roads in the dark.
findings.fix: Correct the figure to roughly four to five hours around the solstice, check the late-February figure (about nine to ten hours), and cite a real daylight source.

findings.quote: Roughly 2.3 million people visit each year ([visitor numbers](https://iceland-weather.example/daylight)).
findings.why: The link text promises visitor statistics, but the address is a daylight/weather page that cannot back a tourist-arrivals count.
findings.fix: Cite a tourism statistics source (such as the national tourist board) with the year of the figure, or remove the number.

findings.quote: We spent six days in January 2026 walking the same three routes in three jacket and boot combinations, noting each evening which items stayed dry and which layers we removed.
findings.why: The section claims notes and dates are summarised, but gives no actual results, dates or per-combination findings, so the testing claim has no verifiable evidence.
findings.fix: Add the real dated test log with per-combination outcomes, or remove the testing claims here and in the description ("layers that worked in our trial").

findings.quote: Northern lights season runs from late August to April, but clear skies are never guaranteed.
findings.why: The season window is a stated figure with no source next to it, though it is broadly consistent with common guidance.
findings.fix: Add a source such as the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast page.
